portal_hypertension.abstract: Management of portal hypertension in children including primary prophylaxis of variceal bleeding is controversial due to limited understanding of mortality risk after first variceal hemorrhage (1VH). This international multicenter study was designed to advance understanding of outcomes after pediatric 1VH. Center-specific characteristics and approaches to portal hypertension were determined at 44 international sites. K-means clustered the centers based upon volume and complexity of approaches [cluster 1 high (n=5), cluster 2 low (n=21), cluster 3 intermediate (n=18]). portal_hypertension.abstract: Liver biopsy is a foundational tool in hepatology, providing direct histologic assessment of hepatic parenchyma. Although noninvasive approaches have substantially reduced the need for biopsy in practice, it continues to play a critical role in diagnosis, staging, and therapeutic decision-making across a broad spectrum of liver disorders. This Expert Practice Opinion (EXPO) document was created by a writing group of subject matter experts appointed by the AASLD Practice Guidelines Committee. Writing group members performed a targeted literature review and created expert opinion statements that were unanimously agreed upon. portal_hypertension.title: When Liver Disease Misleads the Diagnosis: Two Cases of TAFRO Syndrome With Porto-Sinusoidal Vascular Disease.
portal_hypertension.authors: Dassy L, Poletti F, Hafraoui K
portal_hypertension.zhSummary: 该文聚焦门静脉高压症，属于临床研究。核心观点：该英文报道关注最新动态：We report two women with TAFRO syndrome associated with portal-sinusoidal vascul... 临床提示：该英文报道关注最新动态：TAFRO syndrome is a rare inflammatory disorder whose hepatic manifestations may ...
portal_hypertension.abstract: TAFRO syndrome is a rare inflammatory disorder whose hepatic manifestations may mimic decompensated cirrhosis. We report two women with TAFRO syndrome associated with portal-sinusoidal vascular disorder (PSVD), a rare cause of non-cirrhotic portal hypertension. In both cases, liver biopsy excluded cirrhosis and confirmed PSVD. Clinical outcomes were markedly different. One patient achieved sustained disease control with anti-IL-6 therapy and remained stable for more than 6 years, whereas the other developed rapidly progressive and fatal disease.
